name: Crème Caramel With Saffron, Rose and Cardamom

cookwares.name: 9- by 13-inch baking dish or roasting pan to accommodate all 6 ramekins

ingredients.name: saffron threads, plus more to taste
vanillav paste, scraped seeds of 1/2 vanilla pod

instructions.primary_message: For the Caramel: Adjust the oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 300°F. Set six 6-ounce ramekins into a 9- by 13-inch baking dish or roasting pan. In a heavy-bottomed small saucepan, heat sugar and water over low heat, swirling occasionally, until sugar dissolves, about 5 minutes. Don’t stir the caramel, which could make the sugar crystallize.

Once sugar dissolves, turn up heat to high and continue to cook caramel, swirling pan occasionally, until it turns from clear syrup into a dark amber-red caramel. Don’t be tempted to take the pan off the heat too soon—a pale, wishy-washy caramel will make for a lackluster dessert. Quickly pour caramel equally between the 6 ramekins. The caramel will start to set hard as it hits the cold dishes, so work quickly, and turn each ramekin to coat as much of the bottom as possible; set aside.

For the Custard: In a medium saucepan, add the milk and cream. With a mortar and pestle, gently bruise cardamom pods, leaving the seeds in shells. Add bruised pods to milk and cream, and heat over low heat until mixture simmers gently, about 7 minutes. Once simmering, turn off heat and set aside to infuse for 30 to 60 minutes.

Meanwhile, use a mortar and pestle to grind the saffron to a fine powder. After cardamom has infused with milk mixture for 30 to 60 minutes, add saffron powder and stir to combine. Reheat mixture over medium heat until simmering. Swirl in rosewater. If needed, add 2 to 3 teaspoons of the warm infused milk to the mortar and stir to dissolve any residual saffron in mortar, then stir back into saucepan. Adjust seasoning to taste with additional saffron and rosewater, if needed, being careful not to add too much (you can always add more, but you can’t take it away). Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, sugar, and vanilla to combine thoroughly, but avoid overwhisking, which will introduce too much air. Slowly pour hot milk mixture into egg mixture while whisking gently.

Set a fine-mesh strainer over a large bowl or a 4-cup liquid measuring cup. Slowly pour the custard through the fine-mesh strainer to avoid introducing air bubbles. Divide custard mixture evenly between ramekins (about 1/2 cup each).

Pour just-boiled—but not boiling—water (around 180º to 200ºF; 88º to 93ºC) into baking dish or roasting rack around ramekins, until it comes 2/3 of the way up the ramekins; be careful not to splash water into the ramekins as you pour. Carefully transfer to middle rack of oven and bake until custards are just set (they should jiggle slightly in the middle and register 175ºF/79ºC to 178ºF/81ºC on an instant-read thermometer inserted in the center), 20 to 30 minutes. Remove from oven, and, using towels or silicone-coated tongs, carefully transfer ramekins to a cooling rack. Allow custards to cool to room temperature, about 1 hour. Refrigerate until set, uncovered, at least 4 hours.

When ready to serve, run a butter or paring knife under warm water and run along the edge to loosen the flan. Set rimmed serving plates on top of the ramekins, then quickly invert to unmold custards and caramel sauce onto plates. If custards do not release from ramekins, immerse the bottoms of ramekins in a bowl of hot water for 5 to 10 seconds, then attempt to invert onto a plate once more. A gentle shake can help, but don’t go too hard or you’ll risk splitting the custard.
After you’ve finished admiring your beautiful handiwork, garnish each crème caramel with a few fresh raspberries and a sprinkle of pistachio nuts. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: Crème Caramel, Crème Caramel With Saffron, Rose and Cardamom recipe, french dessert

description: This fragrant crème caramel layers saffron, rosewater, and cardamom into a silky baked custard topped with a glossy caramel sauce for the perfect make-ahead dessert.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 2 days 8 hr 45 min to 2 days 5 hr 20 min.

Optional substitutions: water → fresh orange juice; vanillav paste → extract; Chopped toasted pistachio nuts → slivered toasted pistachio nuts

Make-ahead and storage: The crème caramels can be refrigerated in their ramekins, wrapped in plastic, for up to 4 days.
author: Dan Baumgardt
